title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Interpretive Note: Disallowance Reductions while a Monetary Appeal Is Open
content:
A dependency disallowance on an Unemployment Benefit Claims record is booked according to the state of the claimant's Lower Authority Appeal — Monetary Determination on the claim, as the Unemployment Insurance Appeals record shows it: the docket, the appellant (the claimant), the appeal status and the decision outcome.

## The rule

| Claimant's Lower Authority Appeal — Monetary Determination on the claim | Reduction booked |
|---|---|
| Stands filed or scheduled | At the pending-appeal share of 0.5, rounded down to the whole dollar |
| Decided, with the determination reversed | No reduction |
| No such appeal open or reversed | In full |

The pending-appeal share applies last: to the product of the weeks and the allowance decrease, and the result is rounded down to the whole dollar.

## Points of interpretation

- Only an appeal filed by the claimant on the Lower Authority Appeal — Monetary Determination docket, concerning this claim, is read.
- An appeal decided with the determination affirmed, or withdrawn, dismissed or closed, is neither open nor reversed, so the reduction is booked in full.

### Hypothetical figures

A product of 390.00 is booked at 195 while the appeal stands scheduled; a product of 391.60 is booked at 195 (195.80 rounded down).
